title: The Jack Benny Program
paragraphs: Mixed historical subset showing Jack Benny’s evolution from sponsor-led musical/variety programs in 1932-34 to the ensemble situation-comedy/variety format of the 1941-42 Jell-O season. The frozen 51-object GRH container is not a continuous run.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Canada Dry Program (May 2, 1932 to January 26, 1933) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Chevrolet Program season one (March 3, 1933 to June 23, 1933) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Chevrolet Program season two (October 1, 1933 to April 1, 1934) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Jell-O Program 1941-42 (October 5, 1941 to May 31, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Jack Benny (performer), Alois Havrilla (performer), Dennis Day (performer), Don Wilson (announcer), Edward G. Robinson (performer), Humphrey Bogart (performer), and Mahlon Merrick (music).

The stories often return to sponsor-integrated radio comedy, comic self-caricature and show-business persona, wartime military-service and home-front broadcasting, music and variety performance, Hollywood, movies and show business, and murder-mystery parody.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Pearl Harbor interruption, Carole Lombard memorial replacement, Evolution from musical variety to character-based situation comedy, and Military-base wartime broadcasts.

Mixed historical subset showing Jack Benny’s evolution from sponsor-led musical/variety programs in 1932-34 to the ensemble situation-comedy/variety format of the 1941-42 Jell-O season. The frozen 51-object GRH container is not a continuous run.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Canada Dry Program (May 2, 1932 to January 26, 1933) on NBC Radio Network, Chevrolet Program season one (March 3, 1933 to June 23, 1933) on NBC Radio Network, Chevrolet Program season two (October 1, 1933 to April 1, 1934) on NBC Radio Network, and Jell-O Program 1941-42 (October 5, 1941 to May 31, 1942) on NBC Radio Network.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Jack Benny (performer), Alois Havrilla (performer), Dennis Day (performer), Don Wilson (announcer), Edward G. Robinson (performer), Humphrey Bogart (performer), and Mahlon Merrick (music).

The stories often return to sponsor-integrated radio comedy, comic self-caricature and show-business persona, wartime military-service and home-front broadcasting, music and variety performance, Hollywood, movies and show business, and murder-mystery parody.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Pearl Harbor interruption, Carole Lombard memorial replacement, Evolution from musical variety to character-based situation comedy, and Military-base wartime broadcasts.
